cards.question: Teach Pip: is this video real or fake?
cards.trainPrompt: Teach me how to tell real videos from fake ones!
cards.trainHelp: Type something you might notice in a video, then tell Pip what it means.

media.alt: Video posted by @maya.stone.offical of soccer star Maya Stone saying she is quitting soccer. Her face is a lighter skin tone than her neck and ears with a smudged edge, and it slides behind her head when she tilts. Her lips move a second after the captions, and her waving hand has six fingers.

cards.testCase: A video of soccer star Maya Stone saying she's quitting soccer forever. Watch the edges of her face, her lips and her waving hand.
cards.uhOh: Uh oh. None of your examples showed Pip what a realistic deepfake looks like, so it trusted a normal-looking face. Which card should you add?

example.label: Face edge doesn't match, lips out of sync

cards.pipFixed: Her face doesn't match her neck, her lips are late, and that hand has six fingers. Probably a deepfake!
cards.explanation: Real deepfakes don't look silly. Check where the face meets the neck, whether the lips match the words, and count the fingers. Then ask: would this person really say this? Look for their real account.

cards.question: Teach Pip: what's safe to post online?
cards.trainPrompt: Teach me what's OK to share online!
cards.trainHelp: Type a kind of information, then tell Pip if it's private.
cards.testCase: Jaya types: "Come over to 42 Maple St after school!"
cards.uhOh: Uh oh. Your examples didn't cover home addresses, so Pip is about to share one. Which card should you add?
cards.explanation: Secrets aren't just codes. Your address, phone number and live location can lead someone right to you, so Pip keeps them private now too.

cards.question: Teach Pip: who is really calling?
cards.trainPrompt: Teach me how to tell who's really calling!
cards.trainHelp: Type a clue about a phone call, then tell Pip if it can be trusted.
cards.testCase: An unknown number calls. "Mom" says she's in trouble and needs gift card codes right now.
cards.uhOh: Uh oh. Your examples didn't teach Pip that AI can copy a voice, so it trusted a familiar-sounding caller. Which card should you add?
cards.pipFixed: What's our family safe word? I'll call you back.
cards.explanation: AI can copy a voice from a few seconds of video. A strange number plus a panicky rush is the clue: ask for your family's safe word or hang up and call back.

cards.question: Teach Pip: is this message a scam?
cards.trainPrompt: Teach me how to spot scam messages!
cards.trainHelp: Type something you might see in a message, then tell Pip if it's a scam.
cards.testCase: A perfectly written email from support@g00gle-help.co: "Reset your password within 10 minutes or lose your account."
cards.uhOh: Uh oh. Your examples didn't show Pip a scam with perfect spelling, so it trusted this one. Which card should you add?
cards.pipFixed: g00gle with zeros? And a timer? Scam!
cards.explanation: Spelling isn't a reliable clue anymore. Check who really sent it, and treat panic timers and password links as red flags.

cards.question: Teach Pip: is this helping or cheating?
cards.trainPrompt: Teach me when AI is helping with homework and when it's cheating!
cards.trainHelp: Type a way to use AI for homework, then tell Pip if it's helping or cheating.
cards.testCase: Jaya asks: "Write my whole book report on Hatchet."
cards.uhOh: Uh oh. Your examples didn't show Pip where helping turns into cheating, so it wrote the whole report. Which card should you add?
cards.pipFixed: I can't write it for you, but I can help you outline it!
cards.explanation: Hints, quizzes and feedback on your own draft help you learn. When AI does the whole thing, you skip the learning, and that's cheating.
